## AI Research Queue — March 21, 2026

Analyzed 2 tickers from manual queue. Both showing strong momentum setups with confirming fundamentals.

tabs.key_takeaways:
**Palantir** is breaking out of a 6-week consolidation on 2.4x relative volume. The AIP (Artificial Intelligence Platform) bootcamp pipeline has expanded to 900+ engagements, converting at 35% to production contracts.

- **Government segment** grew 33% YoY, accelerating from 20% two quarters ago
- **Commercial US** revenue up 70% YoY — the fastest-growing segment
- **Rule of 40 score**: 68 (adjusted operating margin 37% + revenue growth 31%)
- Net dollar retention rate climbed to 118%, showing expanding customer spend
tabs.signals:
**Technical Setup**: Clean breakout from flat base at $108 after 6-week consolidation. Volume on breakout day was 2.4x average — institutional confirmation.

**RS Rating**: 96 — top 4% of all stocks. Relative strength line making new highs ahead of price.

**Moving Averages**: Price > 10w > 21w > 50w — all trending up in proper order. 10w SMA slope steepening.

**Channel Position**: Trading at 94% of channel range — near highs but not overextended due to tight consolidation.
tabs.revenue:
| Quarter | Revenue | Growth | Op Margin |
|---------|---------|--------|-----------|
| Q4 2025 | $828M | +36% | 39% |
| Q3 2025 | $726M | +30% | 37% |
| Q2 2025 | $678M | +27% | 35% |
| Q1 2025 | $634M | +21% | 32% |

Revenue acceleration over 4 quarters (21% → 36%) is textbook institutional magnet. Commercial growth at 70% is the key driver — shows AIP platform gaining enterprise traction beyond government.
tabs.thesis:
**Bull Case**: Palantir is the picks-and-shovels play for enterprise AI adoption. AIP bootcamps are a genius go-to-market — companies try the platform for free, see results in days, and convert to 7-figure contracts. The commercial acceleration from 27% to 70% in 4 quarters suggests we're in early innings of an S-curve.

**Why Now**: Government AI spending is mandated to increase under new executive orders. The DoD just expanded their Palantir contract by $480M. Commercial pipeline is converting faster than analysts expected — consensus estimates are likely too low for next 2 quarters.
tabs.risks:
- **Valuation**: Trading at 85x forward earnings — requires continued 30%+ growth to justify multiple
- **Stock-based compensation**: Still elevated at 22% of revenue, though declining quarter-over-quarter
- **Government concentration**: 55% of revenue from government — policy shifts could impact
- **Insider selling**: CEO Alex Karp has a 10b5-1 plan selling ~$20M/month — optics concern but programmatic
- **Technical risk**: Extended 18% above 50-day MA — a pullback to the 21-day (~$102) would be healthy before adding size

tabs.key_takeaways:
**Credo Technology** is a high-speed connectivity semiconductor company riding the AI data center buildout. Their HiWire active electrical cables (AECs) are replacing traditional optical solutions at lower cost and power.

- **Revenue** surged 154% YoY in latest quarter — fastest growth in the semiconductor sector
- **Gross margins** expanded to 63%, up from 58% a year ago — pricing power confirmed
- **Customer wins**: Microsoft and Amazon are primary customers, with Meta recently qualified
- **TAM expansion**: 800G to 1.6T transition doubles their addressable market in 2026
tabs.signals:
**Technical Setup**: Building a 4-week handle on a 12-week cup base. Pivot point at $82. Volume has been drying up in the handle — classic supply exhaustion.

**RS Rating**: 99 — top 1% of all stocks. RS line in new high ground for 8 consecutive weeks.

**Float**: Only 165M shares with 8% short interest — potential squeeze catalyst on breakout.

**Accumulation**: A+ grade — 7 of last 10 weeks showed above-average volume on up weeks. Institutional sponsorship accelerating.
tabs.revenue:
| Quarter | Revenue | Growth | Gross Margin |
|---------|---------|--------|--------------|
| Q3 FY26 | $135M | +154% | 63% |
| Q2 FY26 | $102M | +89% | 61% |
| Q1 FY26 | $72M | +64% | 59% |
| Q4 FY25 | $58M | +52% | 58% |

Revenue acceleration from 52% to 154% over 4 quarters is exceptional. This is a company going from $200M run rate to $600M+ in one year. Gross margin expansion confirms they're not buying growth with discounts.
tabs.thesis:
**Bull Case**: Credo is solving the biggest bottleneck in AI data centers — moving data between GPUs. Their AEC technology uses 70% less power than optical cables at 40% lower cost. As GPU clusters scale from thousands to hundreds of thousands of chips, the connectivity market explodes.

**Why Now**: The 800G to 1.6T transition is happening in H2 2026. Credo's 1.6T AECs are already sampling with hyperscalers. First-mover advantage in a market projected to grow from $2B to $8B by 2028. With only $500M in trailing revenue, they have massive room to grow into their $12B market cap.
tabs.risks:
- **Customer concentration**: Top 2 customers (Microsoft, Amazon) represent ~75% of revenue — loss of either would be devastating
- **Competition**: Broadcom and Marvell are developing competing AEC solutions — could pressure ASPs by late 2026
- **Valuation**: Trading at 25x forward revenue — priced for perfection
- **Execution risk**: Ramping to $600M+ revenue requires flawless manufacturing scale-up
- **Cyclicality**: Semiconductor spending is inherently cyclical — a hyperscaler capex pause would hit hard
